### Nested Schema for `spec`

Required:

- `name` (String) TemplateName is the immutable name to track the tempate that was used Would normally specify a QuotaLimit "size" for a tenant

Optional:

- `constraints` (Block List, Max: 1) Constraints are for providing management of resource constraints to workloads - Typically only managed by cluster owners to provide hard resource constraints - Used to prevent noisy neigbor issues in a multi-tenanted environment (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--constraints))
- `namespace_claim` (Block List, Max: 1) NamespaceClaim is the reference for a specific namespace claim that resulted in this object (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--namespace_claim))

<a id="nestedblock--spec--constraints"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.constraints`

Optional:

- `hard_quota` (Map of String) QuotaHard are applied as ResourceQuota objects to all namespaces for a tenant of that type There are the maximun resource usage in total for a namespace e.g.: hardQuota:
  requests.cpu: "1"
  requests.memory: "1Gi"
  limit.cpu: "2"
- `limit_ranges` (Block List) LimitRanges (in the context of constraints) are applied as LimitRanges (using Max) These are the largest values that can be used by a single resource in a namespace They will prevent workloads from using up all resources on a single node (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--constraints--limit_ranges))

<a id="nestedblock--spec--constraints--limit_ranges"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.constraints.limit_ranges`

Required:

- `type` (String) Type of resource that this limit applies to.

Optional:

- `max` (Map of String) Max usage constraints on this kind by resource name.
- `max_limit_request_ratio` (Map of String) MaxLimitRequestRatio if specified, the named resource must have a request and limit that are both non-zero where limit divided by request is less than or equal to the enumerated value; this represents the max burst for the named resource.
